correctness.rationale: The identity f(delta*i,delta*j)=gcd(delta,i+j) with coprime i,j yields an exact Jordan-divisor sum, not an approximation. Möbius inversion proves V_d(y)=y^2/(d zeta(2))*product[p/(p+1)]+O(y log(2y)) uniformly, including the infinite-tail bound from gcd(e,d)<=d. The crude 2y^2/d bound controls the d>T or k>K terms. With T=sqrt(x)/(log x)^3 and K=(log x)^3 the error from the central count is o(x^2), the tails are O(x^2 log log x), and the exact factor identity J2(d)*product p/(p+1)=d phi(d) yields harmonic coefficient 1/zeta(2); thus the result is x^2 log x/(2 zeta(2))+O(x^2 log log x). The included exact script independently reconstructs the Jordan sum for five finite cutoffs; no finite test is mistaken for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Fan--Tóth identify power moments at and above t=2 as a natural gap in a novel two-variable gcd map. The proved t=2 endpoint is a genuine logarithmic transition, with explicit 3/pi^2 leading constant and a global quantitative error over all ordered pairs. The cancellation J2(d)*prod[p/(p+1)]=d phi(d) and the square-root cutoff explain the coefficient; the fact is not a routine finite or arbitrary special-case calculation.
